anchor_line: Grab some paper towels before it drips everywhere.

explanation_en: Use wipe with a direction to explain how to move a cloth or towel.
example_en: Wipe it toward you.
anchor_line: Wipe it toward you.

explanation_en: Step in it means putting your foot into the spill or mess.
example_en: And watch the floor—don't step in it!
anchor_line: Watch the floor—don't step in it!

explanation_en: Sticky describes a surface that feels tacky to the touch.
example_en: The floor is sticky.
anchor_line: The floor is sticky.

expression: one more time with a wet cloth
explanation_en: One more time asks for a repeat; with a wet cloth says what to use.
example_en: Then wipe it one more time with a wet cloth.
anchor_line: Then wipe it one more time with a wet cloth.

explanation_en: Away from names a safer position farther from something.
example_en: Keep your cup away from the edge.
anchor_line: Next time, keep your cup away from the edge.

explanation_en: A natural family phrase for starting a washing or cleaning-up routine.
example_en: Kids, time to wash up before bed.
anchor_line: Leo, time to wash up and get ready for bed.

explanation_en: This covers the steps that happen before going to sleep.
example_en: Go get ready for bed, and I'll find your book.
anchor_line: Leo, time to wash up and get ready for bed.

explanation_en: A short request for a little extra time before stopping an activity.
example_en: Five more minutes? I'm almost finished.
anchor_line: Five more minutes?

expression: I'm almost done with this page.
explanation_en: Use be almost done with something when it is nearly finished.
example_en: I'm almost done with my homework.
anchor_line: I'm almost done with this page.

explanation_en: A compact way to describe a very small amount by comparing its size to a pea.
example_en: Use a pea-sized amount of toothpaste.
anchor_line: Just a pea-sized amount is enough.

expression: Let the brush do the work.
explanation_en: A concise instruction telling someone not to force the movement themselves.
example_en: Hold it gently and let the brush do the work.
anchor_line: Let the brush do the work.

explanation_en: An informal response meaning something is far from finished or correct.
example_en: Are we finished? Not even close.
anchor_line: Not even close.

explanation_en: Use this when a device gives a short buzzing signal after an interval.
example_en: Keep brushing and wait for the buzz.
anchor_line: Wait for the buzz.

explanation_en: A short sequence of two instructions used in this family wash-up scene.
example_en: Spit and rinse, then wash your face.
anchor_line: Spit and rinse.

explanation_en: A very concise household instruction meaning put your pajamas on.
example_en: Pajamas on, then choose a story.
anchor_line: Pajamas on.

explanation_en: A common phrase for the point when the lights are turned off for sleep.
example_en: One story, then lights out.
anchor_line: Then lights out.

expression: I'll walk you through the house.
explanation_en: Walk someone through means to guide them step by step, explaining as you go.
example_en: I'll walk you through the house.
anchor_line: I'll walk you through the house.

explanation_en: The small entrance area just inside the front door of a house.
example_en: This is the foyer.
anchor_line: This is the foyer, and right through here is the living room.

explanation_en: A layout where rooms like the kitchen, dining and living areas flow together without walls between them.
example_en: It's an open-concept layout.
anchor_line: The kitchen and dining area are all open — it's an open-concept layout.

explanation_en: The key question to ask at any viewing: are the fridge, stove and dishwasher part of the rent?
example_en: Are the appliances included?
anchor_line: Are the appliances included?

meaning_zh: 客用洗手间（只有马桶和洗手台）
explanation_en: A small bathroom for guests with only a toilet and a sink — no tub or shower.
example_en: This little one here is the powder room.
anchor_line: And this little one here is the powder room — just a toilet and a sink.

explanation_en: A bathroom attached directly to a bedroom, usually the primary bedroom.
example_en: It has its own ensuite bathroom.

explanation_en: Bathroom counting in halves: a powder room counts as a half bath, so two full baths plus a powder room is 'two and a half baths'.
example_en: Two and a half baths in total.
anchor_line: Three bedrooms, two and a half baths, and a finished basement.

explanation_en: The gas heating unit that warms most Canadian houses; 'kick in' means it starts running.
example_en: That's the furnace kicking in.
anchor_line: That's the furnace kicking in.

expression: Hydro and internet are on you.
explanation_en: 'On you' means you pay for it. In Ontario, hydro means electricity — not water.
example_en: Hydro and internet are on you.
anchor_line: Hydro and internet are on you.

meaning_zh: 硬床垫；支撑感较强的床垫
explanation_en: A mattress with a firmer feel and less sink.
example_en: This one's our most popular firm mattress.
anchor_line: This one's our most popular firm mattress.

explanation_en: Used to say that something is included with a purchase.
example_en: It comes with two free pillows today.
anchor_line: It comes with two free pillows today.

explanation_en: A natural way to confirm that you have decided to buy something.
example_en: This mattress feels right. I'll take it.
anchor_line: I'll take it.

explanation_en: A direct question about same-day delivery.
example_en: Can you deliver it today?
anchor_line: Can you deliver it today?

expression: The earliest we can deliver is...
meaning_zh: 我们最早能送货的时间是……
explanation_en: Used to give the first available delivery time.
example_en: The earliest we can deliver is tomorrow afternoon.
anchor_line: The earliest we can deliver is tomorrow afternoon.

explanation_en: Means every available time slot has already been reserved.
example_en: Our truck is fully booked today.
anchor_line: Our truck is fully booked today.

expression: Could I take it with me now?
meaning_zh: 我现在可以自己带走吗？
explanation_en: A polite way to ask about taking a purchase immediately instead of using delivery.
example_en: Could I take it with me now?
anchor_line: Could I take it with me now?

explanation_en: Means you will organize your own transportation.
example_en: I'll arrange a ride and take it home myself.
anchor_line: I'll arrange a ride.

explanation_en: Means preparing and covering an item so it can be transported.
example_en: We can wrap it up for you.
anchor_line: We can wrap it up for you.

explanation_en: A standard way to tell reception which doctor you are scheduled to see.
example_en: I have an appointment with Dr. Smith at 9:40.
anchor_line: Hi, I have an appointment with Dr. Smith at 9:40.

expression: May I have your health card, please?
meaning_zh: 请出示一下您的健康卡，好吗？
explanation_en: A polite front-desk request for a patient’s health card.
example_en: May I have your health card, please?
anchor_line: May I have your health card, please?

explanation_en: A natural phrase used when handing something to another person.
example_en: Sure. Here you go.
anchor_line: Here you go.

meaning_zh: 您已经完成签到登记了
explanation_en: This confirms that the clinic has completed the patient’s arrival registration.
example_en: Thank you. You’re all checked in.
anchor_line: You're all checked in.

explanation_en: A polite instruction to sit and wait.
example_en: Please have a seat in the waiting room.
anchor_line: Please have a seat.

expression: The doctor will call you shortly.
explanation_en: This tells the patient that the doctor will call their name soon.
example_en: Please have a seat. The doctor will call you shortly.
anchor_line: The doctor will call you shortly.

explanation_en: A natural response when someone calls your name.
example_en: Aria? — That’s me.
anchor_line: That's me.

explanation_en: Teachers use this to open with an update; "report" here means to share news, not to report a problem.
example_en: I'm happy to report that he is doing very well.
anchor_line: I'm happy to report that he is doing very well.

explanation_en: A common teacher phrase for raising a hand, answering questions, and joining class activities.
example_en: He participates actively in class.
anchor_line: He participates actively in class.

explanation_en: A warm compliment teachers give parents; a simple "Thank you" is a perfect reply.
example_en: You should be very proud.
anchor_line: You should be very proud.

explanation_en: "Progress" is a noun, so English uses the fixed phrase "make progress" for improving.
example_en: He's making good progress.
anchor_line: He's making good progress.

expression: Is there anything we should work on at home?
meaning_zh: 在家里有什么需要我们配合的吗？
explanation_en: The single most useful question a parent can ask at a conference; "work on" means to practise or improve.
example_en: Is there anything we should work on at home?
anchor_line: Is there anything we should work on at home?

explanation_en: A polite signal word for a suggestion; whatever follows it is the teacher's main advice.
example_en: I'd recommend reading together for about 20 minutes each day.
anchor_line: I'd recommend reading together for about 20 minutes each day.

explanation_en: A natural, warm response when the teacher shares good news about your child.
example_en: That's great to hear.
anchor_line: That's great to hear.

explanation_en: A moderate, reassuring overall assessment: on track, with room to improve. It does not mean "busy doing something".
example_en: Overall, Ethan is doing OK.

meaning_zh: 达到所在年级的学习要求
explanation_en: The standard school phrase for being at the expected level for the grade.
example_en: He's meeting grade level expectations.
anchor_line: He's meeting grade level expectations.

explanation_en: The most useful follow-up question after a general assessment; "need work" means needs improvement.
example_en: Which areas need work?
anchor_line: Which areas need work?

explanation_en: Understanding and explaining what you read — not just reading the words aloud.
example_en: Reading comprehension is main.
anchor_line: Reading comprehension is main.

explanation_en: The natural everyday phrase for attention drifting during a task.
example_en: He sometimes loses focus during independent work.

explanation_en: A common classroom expression for keeping working on the assigned activity.
example_en: He needs reminders to stay on task.
anchor_line: He needs reminders to stay on task, especially with reading or writing.

explanation_en: To follow how something develops over time, not just check it once.
example_en: How can we keep track of his progress?
anchor_line: How can we keep track of his progress?

meaning_zh: 多一点帮助；多一些支持
explanation_en: A gentle school phrase for extra help in one area. It does not mean the student is failing or behind.
example_en: She just needs a little more support with comprehension.
anchor_line: She just needs a little more support with comprehension.

explanation_en: A balanced summary of general performance before talking about one specific area.
example_en: She's doing well overall.

explanation_en: To progress more slowly than the expected level — the worry behind many parents' questions.
example_en: Do you mean she's falling behind?

explanation_en: "Have trouble" is followed by an -ing verb: have trouble explaining, have trouble sleeping.
example_en: She had trouble explaining why the character made that choice.

meaning_zh: 卡住；遇到困难做不下去
explanation_en: An everyday expression for being unable to move forward with a task.
example_en: Does she ask for help when she gets stuck?

explanation_en: Describes a child who stops talking or asking when something gets hard.
example_en: She tends to go quiet and wait.
anchor_line: She tends to go quiet and wait.

expression: check in in about a month
meaning_zh: 大约一个月后再沟通一次
explanation_en: "Check in" means a short follow-up conversation to see how things are going.
example_en: Let's check in in about a month.
anchor_line: Let's check in in about a month.

meaning_zh: 您一定是 Leo 的妈妈。
explanation_en: A friendly way to identify someone when the context makes you fairly sure.
example_en: Hi, you must be Leo's mom.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: Hi, you must be Leo's mom.

meaning_zh: 班主任；负责本班日常事务的老师
explanation_en: The teacher responsible for a student's homeroom group.
example_en: I'm Ms. Carter, his new homeroom teacher.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: I'm Ms. Carter, his new homeroom teacher.

expression: Leo's told me a lot about your class.
meaning_zh: 他经常跟我说起您的课堂。
explanation_en: A warm way to begin a conversation with a teacher.
example_en: Leo's told me a lot about your class.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: Leo's told me a lot about your class.

expression: Why don't you show your mom…?
explanation_en: A natural, friendly suggestion.
example_en: Why don't you show your mom your desk?
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: Leo, why don't you show your mom your desk?

expression: How is he settling into the new grade?
meaning_zh: 他适应新年级的情况怎么样？
explanation_en: Asks how comfortably a child is adjusting to a new situation.
example_en: How is he settling into the new grade?
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: How is he settling into the new grade?

explanation_en: A gentle way to describe a child's early adjustment.
example_en: It's still early, but he seems comfortable.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: It's still early, but he seems comfortable and is getting used to our routines.

meaning_zh: 逐渐熟悉我们的日常安排
explanation_en: Become familiar and comfortable with repeated schedules and procedures.
example_en: He is getting used to our routines.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: It's still early, but he seems comfortable and is getting used to our routines.

expression: Is there anything we should work on at home?
meaning_zh: 我们在家有什么需要配合练习的吗？
explanation_en: A polite way to ask how the family can support learning at home.
example_en: Is there anything we should work on at home?
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: Is there anything we should work on at home?

explanation_en: An online space where families may receive school updates and homework information.
example_en: I post updates and homework in the parent portal.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: I post updates and homework in the parent portal.

explanation_en: The learning development of one particular student.
example_en: I'd like to ask about his individual progress.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师

explanation_en: Schedule a separate one-on-one conversation.
example_en: We can arrange a private meeting anytime.
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: Open House is mainly for meeting families, but we can arrange a private meeting.

expression: Enjoy the rest of the evening!
meaning_zh: 祝你接下来今晚过得愉快！
explanation_en: A friendly closing when the other person will continue an evening event.
example_en: You too. Enjoy the rest of the evening!
titleZh: 学校开放日：第一次见新老师
anchor_line: Enjoy the rest of the evening.

explanation_en: To collect someone before the usual or scheduled time.
example_en: I'm here to pick up my son early today.
anchor_line: I'm here to pick up my son early today.

explanation_en: Used to explain that you contacted someone before arriving.
example_en: I already emailed his teacher this morning.
anchor_line: I already emailed his teacher this morning.

explanation_en: Used to identify a child's teacher or classroom.
example_en: He's in Miss Brown's class.

explanation_en: A natural way to say that you will contact someone now.
example_en: Let me call the classroom.
anchor_line: Let me call the classroom.

explanation_en: An informal expression meaning very soon.
example_en: They'll send him down in a minute.
anchor_line: They'll send him down in a minute.

explanation_en: Used to tell someone that everything required has been completed.
example_en: You're all set. Have a good day.
anchor_line: You're all set.

explanation_en: To take something to a place and leave it there for someone.
example_en: I'm dropping this off for my son.

explanation_en: To leave something behind at home by mistake.
example_en: He forgot his lunch at home.
anchor_line: He forgot his lunch at home.

explanation_en: The standard first question at a school office.
example_en: What's your child's name?
anchor_line: What's your child's name?

expression: write his name on this label
meaning_zh: 把他的名字写在这张标签上
explanation_en: To mark an item with the owner's name so it reaches the right child.
example_en: Could you please write his name on this label?
anchor_line: Could you please write his name and his teacher's name on this label?

expression: put the label on the lunch bag
explanation_en: To stick the label onto the item itself.
example_en: Should I put the label on the lunch bag?
anchor_line: Should I put the label on the lunch bag?

expression: Make sure it's easy to see.
explanation_en: A gentle instruction to place something where it will be noticed.
example_en: Make sure it's easy to see.
anchor_line: Make sure it's easy to see.

explanation_en: A box at the school office where parents leave items for students.
example_en: You can place it in the drop-off bin over there.
anchor_line: You can place it in the drop-off bin over there.

expression: We'll make sure he gets it.
meaning_zh: 我们会确保交到他手上。
explanation_en: A reassuring way to promise the item will reach the child.
example_en: Okay, we'll make sure he gets it.
anchor_line: Okay, we'll make sure he gets it.

explanation_en: A natural positive comment about food or a drink you can see.
example_en: That looks good—what did you order?
anchor_line: That looks good. What did you order?

explanation_en: Asks which food or drink someone chose at a restaurant or coffee shop.
example_en: What did you order?
anchor_line: That looks good. What did you order?

expression: an iced matcha latte with vanilla
meaning_zh: 一杯加香草的冰抹茶拿铁
explanation_en: A drink name followed by “with” to add a flavour or customization.
example_en: It’s an iced matcha latte with vanilla.
anchor_line: It's an iced matcha latte with vanilla.

explanation_en: A short, natural way to ask about the sweetness of food or a drink.
example_en: Nice. Is it sweet?
anchor_line: Nice. Is it sweet?

expression: A little, but not too sweet.
explanation_en: Describes a mild level of sweetness and reassures the listener that it is not excessive.
example_en: A little, but not too sweet.
anchor_line: A little, but not too sweet.

explanation_en: A friendly response when an idea or description appeals to you.
example_en: That sounds good.
anchor_line: That sounds good. I usually get a latte, but I might try that next time.

explanation_en: Uses “get” naturally to talk about your usual café order.
example_en: I usually get a latte.
anchor_line: That sounds good. I usually get a latte, but I might try that next time.

expression: I might try that next time.
meaning_zh: 我下次可能会试试那个。
explanation_en: Shows interest without making a firm promise.
example_en: I might try that next time.
anchor_line: That sounds good. I usually get a latte, but I might try that next time.

explanation_en: A brief, friendly way to encourage someone to try something.
example_en: You should. It’s really good.
anchor_line: You should. It's really good.

explanation_en: A simple, enthusiastic recommendation for food or a drink.
example_en: You should. It’s really good.
anchor_line: You should. It's really good.

explanation_en: A warm way to thank someone for suggesting something.
example_en: Thanks for the recommendation!
anchor_line: Thanks for the recommendation!

explanation_en: A casual, friendly response to thanks.
example_en: No problem!
anchor_line: No problem!

meaning_zh: 你的狗狗真友善／好亲人！
explanation_en: A warm comment about a dog’s relaxed and social behaviour.
example_en: Oh, your dog is so friendly!
anchor_line: Oh, your dog is so friendly.

explanation_en: Uses singular “they” when you do not yet know whether the dog is male or female.
example_en: What’s their name?
anchor_line: What's their name?

explanation_en: Describes a dog that enjoys friendly contact with unfamiliar people.
example_en: He loves meeting new people.
anchor_line: He loves meeting new people.

expression: Would it be okay if I pet him?
explanation_en: A polite permission question used before touching someone else’s dog.
example_en: Would it be okay if I pet him?
anchor_line: Would it be okay if I pet him?

explanation_en: A friendly way to say that the dog would welcome the attention.
example_en: Of course. He’d love that.
anchor_line: He'd love that.

explanation_en: “Just turned” means the birthday happened recently.
example_en: He just turned three.
anchor_line: He just turned three.

explanation_en: A light neighbourhood question that moves the conversation from dogs to the owners.
example_en: Do you live nearby?
anchor_line: Do you live nearby?

explanation_en: Introduces a related detail or a natural self-introduction.
example_en: I’m Aria, by the way.
anchor_line: Yes, I'm Aria, by the way.

expression: We just moved into the building.
explanation_en: Says that you became a resident of the building recently.
example_en: We just moved into the building.
anchor_line: We just moved into the building.

explanation_en: A standard greeting when meeting someone for the first time.
example_en: Nice to meet you, Aria.
anchor_line: Nice to meet you, Aria.

explanation_en: A casual goodbye when you expect to see someone again in the same area.
example_en: See you around!
anchor_line: See you around.

expression: I think our kids are in the same class.
meaning_zh: 我觉得我们的孩子好像在同一个班。
explanation_en: A natural way to open a conversation by mentioning a likely shared connection.
example_en: I think our kids are in the same class.
anchor_line: I think our kids are in the same class.

explanation_en: A short confirmation question using “right?” at the end.
example_en: Oh, yes. Yes, Ms. Carter’s class, right?
anchor_line: Yes, Ms. Carter's class, right?

expression: How is your child liking the class so far?
meaning_zh: 你的孩子目前觉得这个班怎么样？
explanation_en: Asks about a child’s experience from the beginning of class until now.
example_en: How is your child liking the class so far?
anchor_line: How is your child liking the class so far?

explanation_en: A casual, moderate positive response meaning fairly well.
example_en: Pretty well.
anchor_line: Pretty well.

explanation_en: Describes a mild feeling at the beginning of an experience.
example_en: She was a little nervous at first.
anchor_line: She was a little nervous at first, but she's settling in now.

explanation_en: Means becoming comfortable and familiar in a new place or situation.
example_en: She’s settling in now.

explanation_en: A warm response to positive or reassuring news.
example_en: That’s good to hear.
anchor_line: That's good to hear.

expression: get used to the new routine
explanation_en: Means gradually becoming familiar and comfortable with a new schedule or pattern.
example_en: Mine is still getting used to the new routine.
anchor_line: Mine is still getting used to the new routine.

explanation_en: A simple empathetic comment when someone is adapting to something new.
example_en: It’s a big change.
anchor_line: It's a big change.

explanation_en: Uses “looks like” to describe what appears to be happening, and “head in” for going inside.
example_en: Looks like they’re heading in.
anchor_line: Looks like they're heading in.

expression: Maybe we’ll see you here tomorrow.
meaning_zh: 也许明天还能在这里见到你。
explanation_en: A friendly way to suggest that you may meet again without making a firm plan.
example_en: Maybe we’ll see you here tomorrow!
anchor_line: Maybe we'll see you here tomorrow!

explanation_en: A common friendly goodbye; “You too!” is the natural reply.
example_en: Have a good day! — You too!
anchor_line: Have a good day!

expression: They seem to be having a great time.
meaning_zh: 他们看起来玩得很开心。
explanation_en: A friendly observation based on how the children appear to be enjoying themselves.
example_en: They seem to be having a great time together.
anchor_line: They seem to be having a great time together.

explanation_en: Means that something happened very soon after another event.
example_en: They started playing almost right away.
anchor_line: They started playing almost right away.

expression: Mine usually takes a little while.
meaning_zh: 我家孩子通常需要一点时间。
explanation_en: Uses “mine” to refer naturally to your own child when the meaning is clear.
example_en: Mine usually takes a little while to warm up.
anchor_line: Mine usually takes a little while to warm up.

meaning_zh: 逐渐放松下来；慢慢熟络
explanation_en: Here, means becoming more relaxed and comfortable in a social situation.
example_en: Mine usually takes a little while to warm up.
anchor_line: Mine usually takes a little while to warm up.

explanation_en: A short way to say that you have the same experience.
example_en: Same here.
anchor_line: Same here.

explanation_en: Describes finding another child to join in play.
example_en: It’s nice when they find someone to play with.
anchor_line: It’s nice when they find someone to play with.

explanation_en: A light question about someone’s routine in a shared local place.
example_en: Do you come to this playground often?
anchor_line: Do you come to this playground often?

explanation_en: A casual way to say that something happens fairly frequently.
example_en: Pretty often.
anchor_line: Pretty often.

explanation_en: Refers to a time when a place is not as crowded or active.
example_en: We usually come on weekends when it’s less busy.
anchor_line: We usually come on weekends when it’s less busy.

explanation_en: A conversational phrase for a small number of occasions.
example_en: We’ve only been here a couple of times.
anchor_line: We’ve only been here a couple of times.

explanation_en: A natural way for a parent to explain why they need to pause or leave.
example_en: Oh, I think mine needs me.
anchor_line: Oh, I think mine needs me.

expression: Maybe we’ll run into you again.
meaning_zh: 说不定我们还会再碰到。
explanation_en: A warm, casual goodbye that suggests meeting unexpectedly in the same area again.
example_en: Maybe we’ll run into you again!
anchor_line: Maybe we’ll run into you again!

meaning_zh: 来了很多人；参与人数很多
explanation_en: Describes an event that attracts a good number of attendees.
example_en: This is a great turnout.
titleZh: 学校活动上第一次见面
anchor_line: This is a great turnout, isn’t it?

explanation_en: A tag question inviting agreement with the statement before it.
example_en: This is a great turnout, isn’t it?
titleZh: 学校活动上第一次见面
anchor_line: This is a great turnout, isn’t it?

expression: I didn’t expect it to be this busy.
explanation_en: Expresses surprise that an event or place has more people or activity than expected.

anchor_line: There are three main options: metal braces, ceramic braces, and clear aligners like Invisalign.

explanation_en: A reusable question for comparing several choices.
example_en: What's the difference between them?
anchor_line: What's the difference between them?

explanation_en: “Affordable” describes something reasonably priced, not simply cheap.
example_en: Metal is the strongest and most affordable.
anchor_line: Metal is the strongest and most affordable.

explanation_en: A natural comparative phrase for something that attracts less attention.
example_en: It's tooth-colored, so it's less noticeable.
anchor_line: Ceramic works the same way, but it's tooth-colored, so it's less noticeable.

meaning_zh: 可以摘下，而且几乎看不见
explanation_en: Two useful adjectives for describing clear aligners.
example_en: Aligners are removable and almost invisible.
anchor_line: Aligners are removable and almost invisible.

expression: How much does each one cost?
explanation_en: Use “each one” when asking for the price of several individual options.
example_en: How much does each one cost?
anchor_line: How much does each one cost?

expression: How long does the treatment take?
explanation_en: A standard question about the expected duration of treatment.
example_en: How long does the treatment take?
anchor_line: How long does the treatment take?

expression: Which one would you recommend for him?
explanation_en: A polite way to ask a professional to recommend one of several choices.
example_en: My son is 9. Which one would you recommend for him?
anchor_line: Which one would you recommend for him?

expression: Let's go with the metal ones.
explanation_en: “Let's go with…” is used to confirm a choice after considering the options.
example_en: That makes sense. Let's go with the metal ones.
anchor_line: Let's go with the metal ones.

explanation_en: A useful category phrase for foods that may be unsuitable with braces.
example_en: No sticky or hard foods—no gum, no caramel, no popcorn.
anchor_line: No sticky or hard foods, no gum or caramel, no popcorn.

explanation_en: Use this pattern to ask whether someone can continue eating a specific food.
example_en: Can he still eat apples?
anchor_line: Can he still eat apples?

expression: Cut them into small pieces first.
explanation_en: A clear instruction for changing how a food is prepared.
example_en: Cut them into small pieces first.
anchor_line: Cut them into small pieces first, and no biting into corn on the cob.

expression: no biting into corn on the cob
explanation_en: “Bite into” means to use the front teeth to bite directly into something.
example_en: And no biting into corn on the cob.
anchor_line: Cut them into small pieces first, and no biting into corn on the cob.

explanation_en: A reusable question about whether a routine changes in a new situation.
example_en: How about brushing? Is it different with braces?
anchor_line: Is it different with braces?

explanation_en: A concise instruction using “after every” to show frequency.
example_en: Brush after every meal.
anchor_line: Brush after every meal.

expression: What if the braces rub his cheeks?
meaning_zh: 如果牙套磨到他的脸颊怎么办？
explanation_en: “What if…?” introduces a possible concern and asks what to do.
example_en: What if the braces rub his cheeks?
anchor_line: What if the braces rub his cheeks?

explanation_en: “Keep + -ing” describes something uncomfortable that continues or repeats.
example_en: If a wire keeps poking him, give us a call.
anchor_line: If a wire keeps poking him, or a bracket comes loose, give us a call.

explanation_en: “Come loose” means something attached becomes loose or partly detached.
example_en: If a bracket comes loose, give us a call.
anchor_line: If a wire keeps poking him, or a bracket comes loose, give us a call.

expression: I'm here for a blood test.
explanation_en: The simplest way to say why you came to the lab.
example_en: Hi, I'm here for a blood test.
anchor_line: Hi, I'm here for a blood test.

expression: have an appointment under the name ...
explanation_en: Use “under the name” to say whose name a booking was made in.
example_en: I have an appointment at 10:00 under the name Aria.
anchor_line: I have an appointment at 10:00 under the name Aria.

explanation_en: Clinics and labs confirm your date of birth to check your identity.
example_en: Could you please confirm your date of birth?
anchor_line: Thank you. Could you please confirm your date of birth?

explanation_en: “Fast” here is a verb: to not eat before a test. Answer with how long you have been fasting.
example_en: Did you fast for this test? — Yes, I've been fasting since last night.
anchor_line: Got it. Did you fast for this test?

expression: take a seat in the waiting area
explanation_en: What staff say after check-in while you wait to be called.
example_en: Please take a seat in the waiting area. We'll call you shortly.
anchor_line: Great. Please take a seat in the waiting area.

explanation_en: The phlebotomist asks which arm to draw blood from; answer “Left arm, please.”
example_en: Which arm do you prefer? — Left arm, please.
anchor_line: Hi, Aria. Which arm do you prefer?

expression: roll up your sleeve and make a fist
explanation_en: Two instructions you will hear right before the draw.
example_en: Please roll up your sleeve and make a fist.
anchor_line: Please roll up your sleeve and make a fist.

explanation_en: After the draw, you press on the spot for a few minutes to stop the bleeding.
example_en: All done. Keep pressure on this spot for a few minutes.
anchor_line: All done. Keep pressure on this spot for a few minutes.

explanation_en: “Business days” are Monday to Friday; weekends do not count.
example_en: Get them in 2 to 3 business days.
anchor_line: Get them in 2 to 3 business days.

expression: check them online on our portal
meaning_zh: 在我们的在线门户上查看
explanation_en: Many labs let you see results in an online patient portal.
example_en: You can also check them online on our portal.
anchor_line: You can also check them online on our portal.

explanation_en: How doctors usually open a visit — answer with your main symptom.
example_en: Aria, what's bothering you today?
anchor_line: Aria, what's bothering you today?

expression: I've had a really bad headache for the past two days.
explanation_en: “I've had ... for the past two days” gives the symptom and how long it has lasted in one line.
example_en: Doctor, I've had a really bad headache for the past two days.
anchor_line: Doctor, I've had a really bad headache for the past two days, mostly on the right side, throbbing.

explanation_en: A pulsing pain that comes in beats — a classic word for describing migraine pain to a doctor.
example_en: It's mostly on the right side, throbbing.
anchor_line: Doctor, I've had a really bad headache for the past two days, mostly on the right side, throbbing.

explanation_en: A common symptom that comes with migraines; doctors often ask about it directly.
example_en: Any nausea, or sensitivity to light?
anchor_line: Any nausea, or sensitivity to light?

expression: It got so bad I threw up.
explanation_en: “Throw up” is the everyday spoken way to say vomit; “so bad I ...” shows how severe it was.
example_en: Last night it got so bad I threw up.
anchor_line: Last night it got so bad I threw up, and even turning on the lights hurt my eyes.

meaning_zh: 很像是偏头痛的典型症状
explanation_en: “Typical of” means the symptoms match a condition's usual pattern.
example_en: Those symptoms are pretty typical of a migraine.
anchor_line: Those symptoms are pretty typical of a migraine.

explanation_en: Staying up very late to finish work or a project — stronger than just “stay up late”.
example_en: I've been pulling late nights to finish a project.
anchor_line: I've been pulling late nights to finish a project.

explanation_en: “Prescribe” is what a doctor does when giving you medicine; “relieve” means to ease the pain.
example_en: I'll prescribe something to relieve it.
anchor_line: I'll prescribe something to relieve it, and suggest keeping a regular sleep schedule and cutting back on caffeine.

expression: send a referral to a neurologist
explanation_en: In Canada your family doctor sends a referral before you can see a specialist like a neurologist.
example_en: I can send a referral to a neurologist.
anchor_line: If the attacks keep happening, I can send a referral to a neurologist.

explanation_en: “Covered” means the cost is paid by your health coverage, not out of your pocket.
example_en: It'll be covered under your health card.
anchor_line: It'll be covered under your health card.

explanation_en: A test used to check for a streptococcal throat infection.
example_en: Your strep test was negative.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: Your strep test was negative, and your lungs sound clear.

explanation_en: In medical testing, negative means the condition tested for was not detected — usually good news.
example_en: Your strep test was negative.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: Your strep test was negative, and your lungs sound clear.

explanation_en: A clinician's natural way to describe normal breath sounds during an examination.
example_en: Your lungs sound clear.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: Your strep test was negative, and your lungs sound clear.

explanation_en: In a clinic, viral means caused by a virus — not popular or trending online.
example_en: It's probably viral.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: It's probably viral.

explanation_en: Medicines used to treat bacterial infections; they will not help if the illness is viral.
example_en: So I don't need antibiotics?
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: So I don't need antibiotics?

explanation_en: Fluids is broader than water and is the standard phrase in healthcare advice.
example_en: Get some rest, drink plenty of fluids.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: Get some rest, drink plenty of fluids, and keep an eye on your symptoms.

explanation_en: An everyday expression meaning to monitor something for changes over time.
example_en: Keep an eye on your symptoms.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: Get some rest, drink plenty of fluids, and keep an eye on your symptoms.

explanation_en: Used when symptoms or a condition remain unchanged over days.
example_en: If it's been more than 10 days with no improvement, give us a call.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: If it's been more than 10 days with no improvement, or you start feeling better and then get worse again, give us a call.

explanation_en: Used when someone improves first but then their condition deteriorates.
example_en: You start feeling better and then get worse again.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: If it's been more than 10 days with no improvement, or you start feeling better and then get worse again, give us a call.

explanation_en: A natural phrase for difficulty breathing — and a red-flag symptom.
example_en: Get medical help sooner if you have trouble breathing.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: Yes. Get medical help sooner if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or signs of dehydration.

explanation_en: Signs are observable indications of a condition.
example_en: Get medical help sooner if you have signs of dehydration.
titleZh: 听懂诊断：病毒感染怎么办
anchor_line: Yes. Get medical help sooner if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or signs of dehydration.

explanation_en: The amount of glucose in the blood.
example_en: Your blood sugar is a little higher than last time.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察
anchor_line: Your blood sugar is a little high, but not in the diabetic range.

explanation_en: A test-result range associated with diabetes; being outside it does not by itself explain every health detail.
example_en: It's not in the diabetic range.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察
anchor_line: Your blood sugar is a little high, but not in the diabetic range.

explanation_en: In medical contexts, monitor means tracking a condition or result over time, not merely watching it.
example_en: We'll monitor it.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察
anchor_line: We'll monitor it.

explanation_en: Treatment that needs to begin without waiting.
example_en: No immediate treatment is needed.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察

explanation_en: Used for following changes or progress over time.
example_en: The doctor wants to keep tracking any changes.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察

explanation_en: A general and commonly used term for medicine prescribed or taken for treatment.
example_en: So I don't need medication?
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察
anchor_line: So I don't need medication?

explanation_en: Refers to the present stage of a situation and leaves open the possibility of change later.
example_en: Not at this point.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察
anchor_line: Not at this point.

explanation_en: A common North American expression for laboratory tests performed on a blood sample.
example_en: Let's repeat the blood work in three months.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察
anchor_line: I'd like you to repeat the blood work in three months.

explanation_en: An everyday idiom similar to monitor, often less formal.
example_en: We're keeping an eye on it.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察
anchor_line: It means we don't need to treat it right now, but we do want to keep an eye on it.

explanation_en: Used when a measurement or condition does not significantly worsen or change.
example_en: If it stays stable, we'll continue to monitor it.
titleZh: 血糖偏高，医生说先观察

explanation_en: A direct way to identify the painful area.
example_en: It's my lower back — it's been aching for almost a week.
anchor_line: Hi, doctor. It's my lower back.

expression: It's been aching for almost a week.
explanation_en: Use the present perfect continuous to describe pain continuing until now.
example_en: It's been aching for almost a week.
anchor_line: It's been aching for almost a week.

expression: a dull ache that won't go away
explanation_en: A natural description of persistent pain that is not sharp.
example_en: It's just this dull ache that won't go away.
anchor_line: Just this dull ache that won't go away.

explanation_en: A standard question about when a symptom began.
example_en: When did it start?
anchor_line: When did it start?

explanation_en: A common possible trigger for back pain.
example_en: Did you lift something heavy?
anchor_line: Lift something heavy?

meaning_zh: 睡姿不对；以奇怪姿势睡觉
explanation_en: An informal way to describe an unusual sleeping position.
example_en: Did you sleep in a weird position?
anchor_line: Sleep in a weird position?

explanation_en: A concise way to connect a symptom with an earlier event.
example_en: I moved a mattress on Saturday. It started the day after.
anchor_line: It started the day after.

expression: Is the pain sharp, or more of a dull ache?
meaning_zh: 是刺痛，还是更像隐隐的钝痛？
explanation_en: A question that contrasts two common ways of describing pain.
example_en: Is the pain sharp, or more of a dull ache?
anchor_line: Is the pain sharp or more of a dull ache?

expression: It's just there all the time.
explanation_en: An informal way to say the discomfort is constant.
example_en: It's just there all the time.
anchor_line: Dull, not sharp. It's just there all the time.

explanation_en: A common term for an injury caused by overstretching or overworking a muscle.
example_en: The doctor said it was a muscle strain.
anchor_line: Classic muscle strain.

explanation_en: In Canada, “physio” is a common short form of physiotherapy.
example_en: I'll refer you for physio.
anchor_line: I'll refer you for physio and try not to sit for more than an hour at a time.

expression: a burning sensation in my chest
explanation_en: A natural way to describe a hot or burning feeling in the chest.
example_en: I have this burning sensation in my chest—right here.
anchor_line: I have this burning sensation in my chest right here.

explanation_en: A concise pattern for explaining when a symptom began.
example_en: It started after lunch.
anchor_line: It started after lunch.

explanation_en: Two symptom words used to distinguish different kinds of chest discomfort.
example_en: Is it more like pressure or tightness?
anchor_line: Is it more like pressure or tightness, any shortness of breath, sweating, or pain in your arm or jaw?

explanation_en: A common shortened screening question about difficulty breathing.
example_en: Any shortness of breath, sweating, or pain in your arm or jaw?
anchor_line: Is it more like pressure or tightness, any shortness of breath, sweating, or pain in your arm or jaw?

expression: the burning is coming up my throat
explanation_en: A vivid way to explain the direction of the sensation.
example_en: It feels like the burning is coming up my throat.
anchor_line: It feels like the burning is coming up my throat.

explanation_en: “Could be” presents a possibility without claiming certainty.
example_en: It could be heartburn.
anchor_line: It could be heartburn.

meaning_zh: 如果只是偶尔出现症状
explanation_en: A phrase that limits advice to symptoms that happen only sometimes.
example_en: For occasional symptoms, an antacid may help.
anchor_line: For occasional symptoms, an antacid may help, but follow the directions on the packet.

expression: follow the directions on the package
explanation_en: A standard instruction to check and follow product-specific directions.
example_en: Follow the directions on the package.
anchor_line: For occasional symptoms, an antacid may help, but follow the directions on the packet.

explanation_en: A direct question about how quickly a product takes effect.
example_en: How fast does it work?
anchor_line: How fast does it work?

expression: doesn’t go away or gets worse
explanation_en: A useful pattern for describing a symptom that persists or worsens.
example_en: If the chest discomfort doesn’t go away or gets worse, get urgent medical help.
anchor_line: If the chest discomfort doesn't go away or gets worse, get urgent medical help.

explanation_en: An everyday way to describe a symptom that repeatedly returns.
example_en: If it keeps coming back, see your family doctor.
anchor_line: And if it keeps coming back, see your family doctor.

expression: I'd like to book a flu shot.
explanation_en: The standard polite opener for booking a vaccination appointment.
example_en: Hi, I'd like to book a flu shot, please.
anchor_line: Hi, I'd like to book a flu shot, please.

explanation_en: A screening question to find out how many people the booking covers.
example_en: Is it just for yourself, or for your son as well?
anchor_line: Of course. Is it just for yourself?

explanation_en: A short way to say who an appointment or booking is for.
example_en: It's for me and my daughter.
anchor_line: No, for me and my son.

expression: He's old enough to get it here.
meaning_zh: 他年龄够了，可以在这里打
explanation_en: “Old enough to…” confirms someone meets an age requirement.
example_en: She's old enough to get it at the pharmacy.
anchor_line: He's old enough to get it here at the pharmacy.

expression: Have you both had the flu shot before?
meaning_zh: 你们俩以前打过流感疫苗吗？
explanation_en: A routine question about vaccination history before booking.
example_en: Have you had the flu shot before?
anchor_line: Have you both had the flu shot before?

expression: Any egg allergies, either of you?
meaning_zh: 你们俩有人对鸡蛋过敏吗？
explanation_en: Flu vaccines are screened with this question, because some are produced using eggs.
example_en: Any egg allergies, either of you?
anchor_line: Good. Any egg allergies, either of you?

expression: I have Thursday at four or Saturday at ten thirty.
meaning_zh: 周四四点、周六十点半有空位
explanation_en: How staff offer available slots: “I have [day] at [time] or…”.
example_en: I have Tuesday at two or Friday at nine.
anchor_line: I have Thursday at four or Saturday at ten thirty.

explanation_en: A simple reason for choosing a weekend appointment.
example_en: She has work on weekdays.
anchor_line: He has school on weekdays, and I work.

meaning_zh: 请带上两个人的健康卡
explanation_en: “Bring” plus the item — the standard instruction for what to take to an appointment.
example_en: Please bring your health card.
anchor_line: Please bring both health cards.

expression: Should we come a bit early?
meaning_zh: 我们需要提前一点到吗？
explanation_en: A useful question whenever an appointment involves forms or check-in.
example_en: Should I come a bit early?
anchor_line: Should we come a bit early?

expression: a short form to fill out
explanation_en: “Fill out” is the phrasal verb for completing a form.
example_en: There's a short form to fill out at check-in.
anchor_line: There's a short form to fill out.

expression: if either of you has a fever that day, call us and we'll rebook
meaning_zh: 如果那天你们任何一个发烧，打电话来改期
explanation_en: “Either of you” covers two people; “we'll rebook” means the appointment will simply be moved.
example_en: If he has a fever that day, call us and we'll rebook.
anchor_line: And if either of you has a fever that day, call us and we'll rebook.

explanation_en: Use at before a specific appointment time.
example_en: We have an appointment at eleven.
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: Hi, we have an appointment at ten thirty for flu shots.

meaning_zh: 是用 Aria 的名字预约的。
explanation_en: Use under plus a name when staff need to look up a booking.
example_en: It's under Maya Chen.
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: It's under Aria.

expression: Any bad reaction to a vaccine before?
meaning_zh: 以前打疫苗有过严重反应吗？
explanation_en: A short spoken screening question. The fuller version starts with Have you ever had.
example_en: Have you ever had a bad reaction to a vaccine?
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: Any bad reaction to a vaccine before?

explanation_en: A direct question about how something will feel.
example_en: Will it hurt when you take the bandage off?
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: Will it hurt?

explanation_en: Pinch describes a brief, sharp feeling in this scene.
example_en: You might feel a quick pinch.
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: Just a quick pinch, buddy.

expression: Roll your sleeve all the way up
explanation_en: All the way adds the idea of going as far as needed.
example_en: Could you roll your sleeve all the way up?
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: Roll your sleeve all the way up for me.

explanation_en: Use it on its own when the reason is understood.
example_en: I'll keep the receipt, just in case.
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: Now I need you both to stay in the store for fifteen minutes, just in case.

explanation_en: Use it for looking around a store without a specific purchase in mind.
example_en: We'll browse around while we wait.
titleZh: 带孩子去药房打流感疫苗
anchor_line: Okay, we'll browse around for fifteen minutes.

explanation_en: An everyday exaggeration for being very hungry.
example_en: I skipped lunch, and now I'm starving!
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: I'm starving!

explanation_en: A short, caring way to ask whether someone has had a tiring day.
example_en: Long day at school?
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: Long day?

explanation_en: In this context, hands first is a brief reminder to wash before eating.
example_en: Hands first, then you can grab a snack.
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: Whoa — hands first!

explanation_en: Did you plus the base verb asks whether an action already happened.
example_en: Did you wash your hands before lunch?
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: Did you wash your hands?

explanation_en: A short way to say that something is now clean.
example_en: All clean! Can we start cooking now?
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: All clean!

explanation_en: An invitation to take something that has been offered.
example_en: Help yourself to a cookie.
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: Help yourself.

explanation_en: A reminder to do something less quickly.
example_en: Slow down and take smaller bites.
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: Slow down!

explanation_en: A warning about what could happen when someone eats too quickly.
example_en: Chew first, or you'll choke.
titleZh: 放学回家，先洗手再吃饼干
anchor_line: You'll choke.

expression: I fell down the stairs and hit my head.
meaning_zh: 我从楼梯上摔下来，撞到头了。
explanation_en: One complete sentence that reports what happened — where you fell and what you hit.
example_en: I fell down the stairs and hit my head this morning.
anchor_line: Hi, I fell down the stairs and hit my head.

expression: Should I go to the emergency room?
explanation_en: Ask directly whether the situation needs the ER — the nurse will triage from there.
example_en: He has a high fever. Should he go to the emergency room?
anchor_line: Should I go to the emergency room?

explanation_en: The medical way to say someone passed out or blacked out, even briefly.
example_en: Did he lose consciousness at any point?
anchor_line: Did you lose consciousness?

expression: I feel dizzy, and I threw up once.
explanation_en: Two red-flag symptoms after a head injury. Throw up is the everyday way to say vomit.
example_en: She feels dizzy and threw up twice.
anchor_line: No, but I feel dizzy, and I threw up once.

explanation_en: Vision that is not clear or in focus — a standard screening question after a head injury.
example_en: Any blurred vision or double vision?
anchor_line: Any blurred vision?

meaning_zh: 按 1 到 10 分来打分
explanation_en: How pain is usually rated in Canadian healthcare. Answer with a number: "Maybe a 6."
example_en: How bad is the pain, on a scale of 1 to 10?
anchor_line: How bad is the headache, on a scale of 1 to 10?

explanation_en: After a head injury you may feel worse on the way — have someone take you, or call for help.
example_en: Don't drive yourself. I'll take you.
anchor_line: Don't drive yourself.

explanation_en: For an ER visit in Ontario, your health card is the one document you must bring.
example_en: Do I need to bring anything? — Just your health card.
anchor_line: Just your health card.

explanation_en: After a head injury, someone should stay nearby and watch for changes.
example_en: Have someone stay with you for the first 24 hours.
anchor_line: And have someone stay with you.

explanation_en: Go to the pharmacy and collect medication the doctor has already prescribed.
